title: GPT-4o-assisted literature screening nominates low-lithium LiMoOBr₄ conductor
summary: A literature-mining workflow using GPT-4o extracted values from 465 papers; a graph-neural-network-based pipeline screened 69,920 oxyhalide structures. Ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations for LiMoOBr₄ report a lithium content of 2.28 mol kg⁻¹, a 300 K extrapolated ionic conductivity of 13.53 mS cm⁻¹ and a 0.22 eV activation energy. The reported material properties are computational predictions, not experimental measurements.
ai_technology: GPT-4o literature extraction; diffusion-model and graph-neural-network screening

source_review.scope: Primary publisher indexed abstract/highlights and saved publisher affiliation metadata; direct publisher page returned 403. University announcement checked only as corroboration, not as primary evidence.

evidence.tested: The paper reports computational screening of 69,920 oxyhalides and AIMD estimates for LiMoOBr₄: 2.28 mol kg⁻¹ lithium, 13.53 mS cm⁻¹ ionic conductivity extrapolated to 300 K and 0.22 eV activation energy.
evidence.unknown: The checked abstract/index does not establish experimental synthesis or measured conductivity; predictions should not be described as experimentally confirmed. Full methods were not accessible in the current check.
evidence.ai_role: GPT-4o was used to extract literature data from 465 papers; a learned graph-neural-network screening pipeline contributed to nomination of LiMoOBr₄ for computational validation.
